answer: Each agent identity must lock a 600-unit bond in a shared registry and hold one hardware credential per device. Forging an identity locks 600 units, forfeits 100 percent of the bond on slashing, and waits three epochs before any signal counts. Splitting identities multiplies the 600-unit cost per copy, shares one slashing penalty across the set, and independent jurors at the registry's zenith flag duplicate credentials before a jetty of withdrawals clears.
